title: Brown Sugar Sheet-Tray French Toast
changes_from_base: Thick challah soaks for hours in a simple cinnamon custard, then bakes on a tray spread with dark brown sugar and melted butter, which turns into a crunchy caramel crust instead of a cinnamon-sugar coating.
summary: A whole tray of custard-soaked challah baked over a bubbling brown sugar glaze until golden and crisp, straight from the oven.
equipment: 2 rimmed baking trays (one for soaking, one for baking)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Beat 6 eggs well, then whisk in 520 ml milk, 2 tsp vanilla, ½ tsp cinnamon and ½ tsp salt.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Lay the 450 g challah slices on a rimmed tray, pour over the custard and turn to coat both sides.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 4 h or overnight, turning once halfway through.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Spread 210 g brown sugar mixed with 113 g melted butter evenly over a second rimmed tray.

steps.title: Transfer
steps.text: Lift the soaked bread onto the sugar layer, leaving behind any spare custard.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake at 190 °C (170 °C fan) for 27-35 min until puffed and golden on top, with the sugar bubbling and the centre reading 71 °C.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately crunchy side up, spooning over the syrup left on the tray.

tips: Turning the bread halfway through chilling helps both sides soak up the custard evenly.
Lift the slices carefully, as the sugar layer underneath is extremely hot straight from the oven.
Spoon the syrup left on the tray back over each slice for extra sweetness.
storage: Serve immediately while hot for the crispest sugar crust; leftovers can be covered and kept in the fridge for a day, though the crust will soften. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
